scenes.heading: Speciation
scenes.say: Speciation is how one species splits into two or more new species. It's how the huge diversity of life arose from shared ancestors, and why islands like the Galápagos have so many unique species.

scenes.heading: What is a species?
points: So horses and donkeys are separate species
scenes.say: A species is a group that can interbreed in nature to produce viable and fertile offspring. A horse and a donkey can mate, but the mule is almost always infertile. So they're separate species.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A friend group split between Perth and Melbourne develops different slang
scenes.science: Separated populations develop different gene pools
scenes.breaks: people change slang by choice within a lifetime; allele frequencies change over many generations with no choice involved.
scenes.say: Imagine a friend group where half move to Perth and half stay in Melbourne. They stop chatting daily, so no new slang passes between them. That's a barrier stopping gene flow. Each group picks up its own words. Years later, they hardly get each other's in-jokes. That's like reproductive isolation.

scenes.heading: Allopatric speciation
steps: Isolation: a barrier stops gene flow
scenes.say: Very Interesting Species Arise Repeatedly. Variation exists. Isolation by a geographical barrier stops gene flow. Selection pressures differ, with mutation and drift adding more change. Allele frequencies diverge over many generations. Finally, reproductive isolation: they can't produce fertile offspring together.

scenes.heading: Allopatric vs sympatric

right.title: Sympatric
points: Or a change in breeding time

scenes.say: Allo means other place: a river, mountain or ocean separates the populations. Sym means same place: no barrier. In plants, polyploidy can create a new species in one step, because a triploid offspring is usually sterile.

scenes.heading: Isolating mechanisms
scenes.say: Ask: did a zygote form? Pre-zygotic mechanisms stop mating or fertilisation, like breeding at different times, or different songs. Post-zygotic mechanisms act after, like a hybrid that dies or is sterile, such as the mule.

scenes.heading: Galápagos finches
scenes.question: Why do finches on different Galápagos islands have different beak shapes?
lines: Beaks suited to local food were favoured
scenes.say: Ocean separated the finches on different islands, and each island offered different food. Deep, strong beaks crack hard seeds. Thin, pointed beaks catch insects. Over many generations, one ancestor became many species. That's adaptive radiation.

points: Species: viable, fertile offspring in nature
Speciation needs gene flow to stop
scenes.say: Quick recap. Speciation needs gene flow to stop. Allopatric uses a barrier, sympatric happens in the same place. And isolating mechanisms keep the new species apart. Now try the practice questions!
